title: A Web for Everyone
paragraphs: In March nineteen eighty nine, a young British scientist named Tim Berners-Lee wrote a proposal for a distributed information system at CERN, the European particle physics laboratory near Geneva. His colleagues kept documents on many incompatible computers, so finding and sharing information was slow and frustrating. His idea was to link documents together so that a reader could jump from one to another with a click.

By the end of nineteen ninety, the first Web server and browser were running at CERN. The first website lived on Berners-Lee's own computer and described the project itself. At first, however, it was mostly used by physicists, and few people outside the laboratory had heard of it. Everything changed on thirty April nineteen ninety three.

On that date, CERN released the Web software into the public domain, which meant that anyone could use it freely. Without that decision, the technology might have remained a specialist tool or become the property of a single company. Instead, it spread quickly, and within a few years millions of people were using it. Today the Web is part of everyday life.
